source.citation: Yoder, H. S. & Tilley, C. E. (1962). Origin of basalt magmas: an experimental study of natural and synthetic rock systems. Journal of Petrology 3, 342-532.
source.table: Table 2, 'Chemical analyses and norms of rocks investigated (*) and rocks closely related'
source.file: 1962_Yoder & Tilley_JoP_Origin of basalt magmas-An  experimental study of natural and synthetic rock systems.pdf

transcription.method: pages rendered at 200 dpi with PyMuPDF and read from the images; the PDF text layer (OCR) was used only as a cross-check
verification: every analysis reproduces its printed oxide TOTAL within 0.015 wt% (all 25)
every norm reproduces its printed norm TOTAL within 0.015 wt% (all 25)

conventions.decimal: the printed mid-dot (·) is the decimal point
conventions.columns: n_* columns are the printed CIPW norm; total and n_total are the printed totals

corrections.finding: printed magnetite and ilmenite appear transposed: e.g. no. 10 prints Mt 5.78, Il 2.55, but its Fe2O3 = 1.72 wt% allows at most 2.49 wt% Mt while its TiO2 = 3.02 wt% gives 5.74 wt% Il
printed total 99.86 vs 99.865 from the printed oxides (rounding in the original)
larnite (Cs) and kalsilite (Ks) are printed in the Qz and Or rows with annotations '(Cs)' and '(Ks)'
